title: VPC ops stakeholder brief and dispute matrix
body:
Executive summary:

This brief is a concise operational messaging and rebuttal matrix for pre-sales and solution engineering conversations with regulated buyers (finance, healthcare, public sector) evaluating private VPC or on-prem deployments. Focus: clear control plane language, minimum viable commitments we can make to operations teams, and a quick mapping from common objections to concrete artifacts or deliverables to close the deal.

Guiding principles for messaging to ops/security: keep language concrete, avoid product buzzwords alone, always follow statements with the artifact we can produce (diagram, report, demo, test). Ops people want to see the data flow, control boundaries, and auditability.

Target personas and their priorities:
- CISO / Security Architect: data residency, key custody, audit trail, breach blast radius, third-party risk.
- Platform/Infra Lead: deployment automation, networking patterns, observability, fallback behavior.
- Compliance / Audit Manager: evidence (policies, audits), retention, supplier questionnaires (e.g., SIG, VPAT).
- Engineering Lead (apps): latency, throughput, deterministic failures and rollbacks.

Core messages (short, repeatable):
1) "Control plane where you want it": We offer three control plane models (Redwood-hosted with VPC peering, customer-managed control plane in your cloud account, and on-prem air-gapped control plane). We map each model to specific guarantees (networking, key custody, audit access).
2) "No data persists in vendor-managed storage unless you say so": By default request payloads and KV caches are ephemeral and can be configured to never leave your VPC; logs and audit traces are exportable to your SIEM.
3) "Bring your key, keep full custody": BYOK integrations (Cloud KMS/HSM, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) + support for rotating and revoking keys without vendor access.
4) "Performance parity and local failover": Dedicated capacity options and local inference modes ensure latency SLAs are met even with private deployments.

Control plane options — plain language and what to promise:
- Managed (Redwood-hosted) control plane: Fastest onboarding, Redwood manages orchestration meta-state (deployments, billing, rollouts). Network: PrivateLink/VPC peering recommended. Data: customer data plane stays in customer's VPC, control plane communicates over mTLS with mutual auth. Artifacts to provide: network flow diagram, SOC 2 report, PrivateLink setup guide.
- Customer-managed control plane: We ship a lightweight control plane service you run in your account (container/managed service). You retain admin-level access, logs, and policies. This model minimizes third-party service access. Artifacts: deployment templates (Terraform/Helm), KMS integration guide, single-tenant service SLA.
- On-prem / Air-gapped control plane: Full offline installable control plane for regulated environments. Requires joint installation runbook and periodic patching cadence. Artifacts: install checklist, on-site runbook, acceptance test plan.

Data flow & least-privilege wording ops like to hear:
- "Control metadata flows over mTLS; payloads and model artifacts are pinned to your VPC/GCS/S3 bucket unless you request otherwise."
- "We never store customer prompt content in vendor-managed databases by default — persistent storage is customer-controlled and optional (configurable per-model route)."
- "Audit logs are exported in near-real-time to your logging endpoint (S3, Splunk, Datadog) and are retained under your policy."

Objection -> Rebuttal -> Required artifact (owner) matrix (quick reference):
- Objection: "We cannot allow any vendor control plane in our cloud."
  Rebuttal: "We support a customer-managed control plane you run inside your account; it's functionally equivalent and gives you admin access and log ownership."
  Artifact: Terraform/Helm deployment manifest + runbook (infra eng).

- Objection: "Vendor could exfiltrate prompts or models."
  Rebuttal: "BYOK + data plane isolation + optional disabled telemetry. Admin logs show every control-plane operation; we can provide audit demonstrations."
  Artifact: BYOK integration guide + audit demo checklist (security eng).

- Objection: "We require FedRAMP/SOC2 evidence."
  Rebuttal: "We provide our SOC 2 Type II report, a FedRAMP readiness pack (where applicable), and a supplier questionnaire response packet."
  Artifact: SOC 2 report + questionnaire pack (compliance).

- Objection: "Latency unacceptable for inference close to users/data."
  Rebuttal: "Dedicated GPU pools deployed in your VPC and local inference options guarantee low tail latency; we can run a pilot with your representative workload."
  Artifact: Pilot run plan + baseline perf report (solutions eng / infra).

- Objection: "We need to demonstrate revocation/rotation of keys without vendor access."
  Rebuttal: "Rotation can be performed by you; vendor has zero access to plaintext keys when BYOK/HSM is used. We provide a key-rotation dry run document."
  Artifact: Key rotation runbook and test script (security).

- Objection: "How does rollback/incident handling work when you don't control the control plane?"
  Rebuttal: "Customer-managed control plane includes built-in rollbacks; for managed control plane we provide a documented incident API and signed runbooks; for on-prem we provide joint on-call integration steps."
  Artifact: Incident runbook + API spec for incident commands (sre/solutions).

Competitive notes (short):
- Primary competitor pattern A: Heavily marketed "zero customer install" with limited BYOK and telemetry opt-out. Counter: highlight ability to run the control plane in-customer with parity and provide deployment artifacts.
- Competitor B: Self-hosted but built for infra teams only (no strong developer ergonomics). Counter: emphasize our unified API + rollout tooling + canary/A-B testing even in private installs.
- Competitor C: Managed service with ambiguous audit exports. Counter: call out our export-first auditing and demoability.

Rapid rebuttal snippets (for Slack or email threads):
- To Security: "We can provision a customer-managed control plane in your account this sprint — we use your KMS and export audit logs to your S3. I'll drop the Terraform (TF) module and a runbook for your infra team to validate."
- To Infra: "We support PrivateLink and peered VPCs; pilot uses a single dedicated GPU pool in-region and the same model binary you run in prod."

Mini playbook for demos / POC runs:
1) Pre-call: share architecture diagram and SOC 2; ask for network contact and KMS owner.
2) Day 0: run a smoke deploy of the customer-managed control plane into their UAT account (Terraform + Helm).
3) Day 1: onboard 1 model route, enable audit export to their S3, run sample inference workload and capture latency/throughput.
4) Day 3: run key rotation exercise and show audit logs in their SIEM.

Open questions / known edge cases (for internal follow-up):
- We need a standardized supplier questionnaire (SIG-lite) tailored for regulated buyers — owner: compliance.
- On air-gapped installs, define patch cadence and emergency patch playbook for critical CVEs — owner: release engineering.
- Decide SLA language for customer-managed control plane (what we guarantee vs what we recommend customers run).

Next steps (short list):
- Solutions eng to produce a 1-page customer-managed control plane one-pager and attach Terraform examples (deadline: 2025-11-22).
- Compliance to produce SIG-lite and a pre-filled vendor responses pack (deadline: 2025-11-29).
- Sales enablement: create two 5-slide decks (technical and executive) for regulated buyers (deadline: 2025-12-05).

Notes on tone and style for SEs and AEs: never say "we will" without naming the artifact. Replace vague terms ("secure", "private") with concrete phrases ("BYOK with CloudHSM", "audit logs exported to S3 with customer lifecycle policies").

Appendix — quick artifact checklist to have on hand for buyer meetings:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- BYOK/HSM integration guide
- Terraform/Helm quickstart for customer-managed control plane
- Network diagram templates (PrivateLink, VPC peering, on-prem tunnelling)
- Incident runbook summary and RACI
- Pilot plan and perf-sample report template

End of brief.

(Tone: working draft — share feedback and missing edge cases here. Mark items you can own in the linked artifacts list.)
